title: P2DFlow: A Protein Ensemble Generative Model with SE(3) Flow Matching

nodes.text: P2DFlow is an SE(3)-equivariant flow matching generative model that predicts protein structural ensembles, interpolating backbone frame translations (in R3) and rotations (in SO(3)) along an optimal-transport path and predicting torsion angles with an MLP.
nodes.evidence: we propose a new framework that samples protein ensembles via a SE(3) equivariant flow matching model named P2DFlow

nodes.text: P2DFlow uses a strong prior consisting of ESMFold predictions perturbed with Gaussian noise on coordinates, rather than a Gaussian or harmonic prior, to introduce more precise biases in bond lengths and angles as initial iteration values.
nodes.evidence: we use a strong prior, ESMFold predictions with perturbations of coordinates... the stronger prior that we use guides the model to generate accurate structures by introducing more precise biases in bond lengths and bond angles

nodes.text: An additional 'approximate energy' dimension is introduced by projecting MD ensembles onto a 2D plane of radius of gyration and RMSD, computing Gaussian kernel density, and converting density to energy via the Boltzmann equation; this conditions generation to distinguish conformations of distinct energies.
nodes.evidence: we introduce a new dimension called 'approximate energy', which maps MD results onto a low-dimensional plane and uses the density to represent probability... uses the Boltzmann Equation to convert the density values into 'approximate energy' values

nodes.text: The SE(3)-equivariant network architecture stacks Invariant Point Attention (IPA) and E(n) equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) modules over a residue graph, with ESM-2 providing initial node and pair representations.
nodes.evidence: the stacking of Invariant Point Attention (IPA) module and E(n) equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) module

nodes.text: P2DFlow's strong ESMFold-perturbation prior differs fundamentally from AlphaFlow, which uses a harmonic prior and relies on AlphaFold/ESMFold as the main structure-controlling component, whereas P2DFlow uses a separate SE(3)-equivariant block to adjust structure.
nodes.evidence: This approach differs significantly from AlphaFlow, which uses harmonic prior and relies on AlphaFold or ESMFold as the main component to control structure. In contrast, P2DFlow employs ESMFold predictions with perturbations as a stronger prior and utilizes a new SE(3) equivariant block

nodes.text: AlphaFlow encounters challenges generating non-existent intermediate states between energy minima, and the 'approximate energy' conditioning is designed to avoid generating such non-existent intermediate states.
nodes.evidence: It guides the model in generating conformations with distinct energies, thereby avoiding the generation of non-existent intermediate states

nodes.text: STR2STR's diffusion approach suffers large variability in predicted results, making it hard to focus on a particular low-energy conformation, possibly due to inconsistencies in its prior distribution between training and sampling.
nodes.evidence: the large variability in its predicted results makes it difficult to focus on a particular low-energy conformation. This may be due to inconsistencies in its prior distribution during training and sampling processes

nodes.text: A prior distribution closer to the target data distribution yields superior performance, which is cited as the rationale for using perturbed ESMFold predictions as the prior.
nodes.evidence: Previous studies has shown that the prior distribution closer to data distribution which needs to be learned can lead to superior performance

nodes.text: Trained and evaluated on the ATLAS MD dataset, P2DFlow outperforms AlphaFlow and STR2STR on PWD JSD, RMWD W2, RMSF, RP IoU, and Weak Contacts Jaccard, indicating more realistic reproduction of the physical-space distribution of structures.
nodes.evidence: P2DFlow performs better than AlphaFlow and STR2STR in PWD J, RMWD W2, RMSF, RP IoU and Weak Contacts Ja

nodes.text: P2DFlow reduces RMWD W2 to 23.020 versus 33.628 for AlphaFlow and 78.246 for STR2STR, and shows fewer bad outliers with narrower result distributions, indicating more stable predictions.
nodes.evidence: RMWD W2 ... 78.246 33.628 23.020 ... there are a few bad outliers predicted by AlphaFlow and STR2STR, whereas P2DFlow does not exhibit such issues

nodes.text: Ablation shows the 'approximate energy' dimension significantly aids in constructing the protein conformation distribution.
nodes.evidence: the ablation experiment shows that the 'approximate energy' significantly aids in constructing the conformation distribution of proteins

nodes.text: The training loss combines a vector-field term (weighted by 1/(1-min{t,0.9})^2 to prevent loss explosion) on translation and rotation with an auxiliary all-atom coordinate and distance-matrix loss, with pre-alignment of x0 and x1 via the Kabsch algorithm.
nodes.evidence: We modify the loss function by substituting 1/(1-t)^2 with 1/(1-min{t,0.9})^2 to prevent the loss from exploding... we conduct a pre-alignment to align x0 and x1 using the Kabsch algorithm
